SKIN. [46] [Chel.]
Skin dry, hot, or shining red and moist, itching intolerably.
Skin cold and dry.
Skin cool and rough. θ Intestinal catarrh.
Yellow, yellowish-grey, wilted skin. θ Hepatic affections. θ Intestinal catarrh. θ Valvular disease. θ Typhus.
Yellow color of skin, neck, chest and hands.
Acute jaundice.
Itching of skin.
Burning pain like nettles, preceding an eruption like measles.
Bright red, lentil-sized, round spots on face, on awaking in morning.
Red, round, burning spots on forearm.
Red, ring-shaped, confluent spots, skin seems mottled. θ Acute rheumatism.
Red and painful pimples and pustules on various parts.
Eczema.
Red, miliary eruption on neck, chest and arms. θ Acute rheumatism.
Scabs, exuding moisture and scaling off.
Old putrid spreading ulcers.
A large superficial ulcer behind left ear, with reddish, fetid discharge.
Eruptive diseases depending chiefly on disorganization of skin.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Chel.]
Melancholic, choleric temperaments with bilious tendencies and complications.
Suits every age, sex and temperament, but particularly spare subjects disposed to abdominal plethora, cutaneous diseases, catarrh or neuralgia.
Blonde, pale, gentle girls, with inflammation of lungs.
Adapted to children with capillary bronchitis and liver complaints.
Children with intestinal catarrh, followed by great emaciation and feebleness.
Bright-colored diarrhœa, with children.

RELATIONS. [48] [Chel.]
Antidoted by : Acon., when the circulation becomes excited ; acids, wine and coffee restrict its action.
It antidotes : Bryon.
Compatible : Arsen., Bryon., Cor. rub. (pertussis), Ipec. (spasm of glottis), Ledum, Sulphur (hepatized lung).
Compare : Acon., Arsen., Baryta, Bellad., Bryon., Calcar., Capsic., Chelerythrin, Chen. ant., Cinchon., Corall. (whooping cough), Gambog. (diarrhœa), Graphit., Ignat., Lycop. (liver ; pneumonia, one foot cold), Mercur. (pneumonia, with liver complications), Nitr. ac., Nux vom., Opium (family relation), Phosphor. (chest, yellow diarrhœa), Podoph. (liver), Pulsat., Rhus tox., Sanguin. (family relation), Selen., Sepia, Silic., Spigel., Sulphur and Viol. od.
